GUIDED WATCH TIMING

Find the beat.

Get a clear signal. Measure a baseline. Make one small adjustment.

NO SOURCE
DEMO SIGNAL Generated audio. These are not readings from your watch.

01 / SET UP

Start at the microphone.

A wired iPhone headset mic can work. Place its opening very close to the case edge or crown. Light contact can help if it causes no rubbing. Support both so they stay still.

Build up power through normal wear or gentle rocking. Move the watch away from laptop speakers.

The case can stay open while adjusting. A hat can screen room noise. Keep fabric clear of the movement and mic. Audio stays on this device.

02 / FIND SIGNAL

Look for repeating clicks.

The 7009A makes six beats per second. Look for evenly spaced vertical marks in the spectrogram.

  1. Keep fingers, the cable and the desk still.
  2. Try another contact point if clicks are faint.
  3. Keep noise reduction and auto gain off where possible.
The filter selects the click’s audio frequencies. It does not filter at the six-beats-per-second repetition rate.

03 / MEASURE

Let the reading settle.

Measure for 60 seconds without moving the watch. Repeat in the same position before adjusting.

A usable signal and at least 32 seconds are needed to save a baseline.

04 / ADJUST

One change at a time.

Measure a stable baseline first.

The regulator adjusts rate. Follow its scale pointer: + speeds up; − slows down. Left/right depends on how the movement is rotated.

How much? There is no fixed seconds/day per millimetre or degree. A repeatable before/after reading and a known movement amount are needed to estimate sensitivity. A loose or temporarily held stud prevents reliable calibration.

Spring block: the stud holder carries the hairspring’s outer attachment and adjusts beat error. The displayed milliseconds are an unsigned magnitude, so they cannot choose a direction. Secure the stud with its proper screw before adjusting the holder.

With the back open, photograph the starting position. Under magnification, make a barely visible nudge on the regulator’s metal edge with blunt pegwood. Keep the mic and tool clear of the balance and hairspring. Take a final reading after closing the case.

Never force a stop. If a large loss persists at the + limit, or the watch stops intermittently, it needs inspection.
